findings.title: Payload-size heuristics are emitted as evidence of task-specific over-fetch and compounded cache reads
findings.what: The only cited artifact is resultBytes, but the detector states that calls pulled more than the task used, that a targeted alternative would have been smaller, and that the excess was cache-read on every later turn. Result size alone establishes none of task usage, an actually available smaller slice, or the number of subsequent model turns. The related baseline helper confirms the compounded value is a projection from later tool-call count, not observed cache-read attribution.
findings.fix: Describe these outputs explicitly as heuristic candidates and a projected upper bound, remove the observational claim that a targeted alternative was smaller, and do not book reclaim unless turn-level cache attribution or another observed reuse field supports it.
findings.acceptance: A fixture containing a large final/necessary Read or multiple tool calls within one model turn produces no observed over-fetch/reclaim claim; any remaining projection is labeled as an estimate with provenance naming the heuristic fields and assumptions.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the cited recommendation/provenance lines and the directly related baseline toolPayloadRightSizing implementation. It derives excess from fixed byte thresholds and multiplies by subsequent tool-call count; it does not observe task usage, alternative-result size, or subsequent model-turn cache reads.

findings.title: Unattended entrypoint is insufficient evidence for a booked Batch API saving
findings.what: Every sufficiently large sdk-* session is assigned a 50% estSavingsUsd and booked reclaim. The only eligibility evidence is unattended entrypoint plus optional schedule events. Neither field proves the workload accepts Batch API semantics or up-to-24-hour latency; the action itself acknowledges this still needs confirmation. Consequently the booked aggregate can count savings for latency-sensitive automation.
findings.fix: Require an explicit observed/configured batch-eligible or async-tolerant signal before emitting estSavingsUsd/reclaim. Without it, emit only a non-booked tier-0 opportunity ceiling and state that eligibility is unverified.
findings.acceptance: A token-heavy sdk-* session without explicit async/batch eligibility has no estSavingsUsd or reclaim; a fixture with the eligibility artifact books exactly 50% of standard input/output cost, excludes cache pools, and cites that artifact and field in provenance.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read selection, reclaim, action, attribution, and provenance. No field beyond sdk-* entrypoint and scheduledFires establishes async tolerance, while the unconditional reclaim is constructed before the copy tells the user to confirm it.

findings.title: All 1-hour cache writes are booked as recoverable despite missing reuse evidence
findings.what: The calculation includes every 1-hour cache-write token and books the full 1h-to-5m price delta. It never examines reuse timing or cache reads, even though its action makes recoverability conditional on context not being reused beyond five minutes. Legitimately reused 1-hour entries therefore inflate estSavingsUsd and reclaim.
findings.fix: Gate booked savings on reproducible evidence that each write received no reuse after five minutes, or downgrade the current amount to a non-booked maximum exposure estimate. Add structured provenance for the token, pricing, and reuse fields.
findings.acceptance: A fixture with a 1-hour write reused after a greater-than-five-minute gap contributes zero booked savings; an evidenced non-reused write contributes only its re-derived rate delta, and the returned recommendation contains structured provenance identifying the reuse artifact and fields.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read the complete calculation and return object. The loop consumes only cacheCreation1hTokens, cacheCreationTokens, model, and sessionId; no reuse field is consulted, yet the computed delta is unconditionally exported and reclaimed.

findings.title: Zero same-session cache reads does not prove the full 1-hour write was waste
findings.what: The detector labels every 1-hour write in a session with zero cache-read tokens as deterministic concrete waste and exports the entire write cost as savings. This observation does not establish that the cache entry was never reused outside that session, after the captured interval, or that a shorter-cache alternative would have avoided the full write cost. The arithmetic measures spend correctly but the recoverability inference is unsupported.
findings.fix: Report this as an unverified candidate or maximum exposure unless cache-key/lineage and time-window evidence proves non-reuse. Do not set estSavingsUsd from same-session zero reads alone, and date any incomplete historical observation as of the capture boundary.
findings.acceptance: A fixture with a 1-hour write and zero same-session reads yields no booked savings and no 'concrete waste' claim absent explicit non-reuse evidence; with complete lineage/time-window evidence, only proven unused writes are counted and provenance cites those fields and the observation boundary.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read filtering, arithmetic, action, savings export, and provenance. The sole predicate is cacheCreation1hTokens > 0 plus same-session cacheReadTokens === 0; the code has no cache lineage or observation-completeness evidence capable of proving non-reuse.
